headline: Credit finally cracked — HY +9bp, CCCs +19bp — while the 3-month bill at 4.33% prices a Fed hike into a 21% one-month collapse in crude.
summary: Yesterday the pain was in hard assets. Today it moved into the capital structure. High-yield OAS widened 9bp to 3.43 (94th percentile), CCCs added 19bp to 13.29 after a +302bp three-month blowout, and the quiet part got loud: IG at 0.92 and BBB at 1.15 are both at one-month move z-scores above 1.0 (BBB z=1.11, 92nd percentile). That is the opposite of yesterday, when CCCs tightened 6bp and the credit tape was the reason to stay long. HYG is rolling over, LQD is -1.1% on the week and at the 21st percentile of its 52-week range. Equities papered over it — SPX only -0.2% to 7,323.6, NDX +0.4%, RUT +0.5%, N225 +1.2% — but the Dow fell 1.1% and the sector tape underneath was ugly: XLF -1.9%, XLU -1.6%, XLV -1.4%, with UNH -5.4%, NKE -6.3%, TSM -3.7%, ORCL -3.4% and CEG -3.5%.

Commodities took a fourth leg down and the reason is supply, not just the AI unwind. WTI -4.8% to 81.89 and Brent -4.9% to 88.61 on a 3.4m-barrel US crude build and surplus math; WTI is now -21.0% on the month with a one-month z of -2.09. Copper -4.4% to 5.7115 (z=-2.02, -12.6% on the month), gold -2.8% to 3,756 and still pinned at the 0th percentile, silver -3.4%, platinum -3.3%. DBC's monthly move is z=-2.27. The deflationary impulse is now in the market's own pricing: 10-year breakevens 2.19 (z=-1.10, 3rd percentile) and 5-year 2.23 (12th). And yet the front end is pricing tightening, not easing — the 3-month bill sits at 4.33%, a full 45bp above effective fed funds at 3.88%, the 2-year at 4.80% is +61bp in three months, and the 10-year real yield is 2.89%, 27.9% above its 200-day at the 95th percentile. Falling breakevens plus sticky nominal yields is passive tightening, and 2s10s at 27bp (z=-0.68, acceleration -1.02) is flattening to say so. The dollar is the transmission belt: DXY 103.80 at the 100th percentile, USDCHF and USDCAD also at 100, EURUSD 1.0982 at zero, and USDMXN +2.6% in a single session on Fed-hike chatter — the biggest FX move on the board today, with Brazil's USDBRL finally pausing (-0.1%) after a +14.1% month (z=3.97).

The offsets are real and they are the reason this is a rotation, not yet a rout. Gasoline is -23.6% on the month, a direct rebate to the consumer and to freight: UPS +14.8% (z=1.87), FDX +9.0%, MCD +13.5% (z=2.52), COST +12.4%, HD +9.5%, WMT +7.3%. Mortgages at 7.11%, -29bp on the month with acceleration z=-2.36, have ITB +6.2% and XHB/SPY at z=1.60. Labour refuses to break: claims 200k, continuing claims 1.697m at the 1st percentile, JOLTS 7,523 and +4.6%, unemployment 4.1%. Breadth still has not confirmed the index damage — equal-weight/cap-weight z=2.46 with acceleration 1.69, transports/S&P z=2.12, and small caps outperformed again today. Leadership has simply emigrated: India's Sensex +10.4% on the month (z=2.46, acceleration 1.74) with INDA +8.9% and relative strength +13.5%, while Taiwan is -14.9% and Korea -12.3%.

Net: risk regime unchanged at -19, but the composition is worse. The rates composite improved slightly to -51 and the dollar composite deteriorated to -53 from -48. Two accelerations to respect, both bearish: credit decompression into a vol curve that is still inverted (VIX 24.56, +40.4% on the week despite today's -3.5%; VIX3M +23.9% on the month at z=1.45; VIX/VIX3M 1.0111) with SKEW at z=-1.78, meaning nobody owns tails into a widening spread cycle. And global cyclicals are snapping — COPX -18.3% on the month, FCX -20.5%, XME -11.6%, CAT -21.7% (z=-2.48, 6th percentile). Crypto remains the purest leverage gauge and it keeps bleeding: BTC 63,062 (-24% on the month), MSTR -6.3% today, COIN at the 0th percentile. Own the deflation beneficiaries, short the credit and the cyclical beta; do not fight the dollar.

good.text: Energy is handing cash back to the consumer: WTI -4.8% to 81.89 (-21.0% on the month) and gasoline -23.6%, showing up directly in UPS +14.8%, FDX +9.0%, MCD +13.5%, COST +12.4% and HD +9.5%.

The inflation tail is being priced out: 10-year breakevens 2.19 (z=-1.10, 3rd percentile) and 5-year 2.23, with DBC's monthly move at z=-2.27. If the Fed ever looks at market pricing instead of October core CPI, this is the dovish pivot fuel.
Housing is the one rate-sensitive sector improving: 30-year mortgage 7.11%, -29bp on the month with acceleration z=-2.36, starts +9.9%, ITB +6.2% and homebuilders/S&P at z=1.60.
Breadth still will not confirm the index damage — equal-weight/cap-weight z=2.46 (acceleration 1.69), transports/S&P z=2.12, and the Russell +0.5% today against the Dow -1.1%.
The labour market is intact: claims 200k, continuing claims 1.697m at the 1st percentile, JOLTS 7,523 (+4.6%), unemployment 4.1%. This is a price shock, not a demand collapse.
New leadership is visible and trending: Sensex +10.4% on the month (z=2.46, acceleration 1.74), INDA relative strength +13.5%, plus Mexico's IPC +13.2% vs S&P over three months and DAX +5.9%.

bad.text: Credit decompressed for real today — HY OAS +9bp to 3.43 (94th percentile), CCCs +19bp to 13.29 after +302bp in three months — and the investment-grade complex joined, with IG z=1.04 and BBB z=1.11. That is a reversal of yesterday's tightening.

The front end is pricing a hike into a commodity crash: the 3-month bill at 4.33% is 45bp above effective fed funds at 3.88%, the 2-year is 4.80%, and the 10-year real yield 2.89% sits 27.9% above its 200-day at the 95th percentile.
The dollar is still the wrecking ball: DXY 103.80 at the 100th percentile, EURUSD 1.0982 at the 0th, USDMXN +2.6% in one session, EM FX basket -2.0% on the month, after USDBRL's +14.1% (z=3.97).
Global cyclicals are breaking, not correcting: copper -4.4% (z=-2.02), COPX -18.3% on the month, FCX -20.5%, XME -11.6%, CAT -21.7% (z=-2.48, 6th percentile).

Volatility has repriced higher across the curve with no tail protection owned: VIX 24.56 (+40.4% on the week), VIX3M +23.9% on the month (z=1.45), term structure inverted at 1.0111, SKEW z=-1.78, MOVE +37.7% over three months.
Leverage keeps liquidating: BTC 63,062 (-24% on the month), SOL -30.9%, MSTR -6.3% today and -29.5% on the month, COIN at the 0th percentile, ARKK -13.2%.

trades.name: Credit decompression: Treasuries over junk
trades.line: Long IEF vs short HYG as HY/CCC spreads reprice
trades.expr: Buy IEF, short HYG, dollar-neutral. Overlay: buy 3-month HYG 74 puts if you want convexity rather than carry drag.
trades.thesis: Spreads are decompressing from a historically tight base while the macro impulse (crude -21% on the month, breakevens at the 3rd percentile, CCCs +302bp in three months) is squarely deflationary for leveraged issuers. Treasuries win on both legs: duration catches the growth scare, HYG catches the spread.
trades.trigger: HY OAS +9bp to 3.43 (94th percentile) and CCCs +19bp to 13.29 today, reversing yesterday's 6bp tightening; IG one-month move z=1.04 and BBB z=1.11 mean the widening is no longer confined to junk; HYG is rolling over while VIX is +40.4% on the week.
trades.stop: HY OAS back below 3.25 with CCCs tightening two sessions in a row, or the combined position -3%.
trades.target: HY OAS 4.00+, CCCs through 1,400bp; +5% on the pair.

trades.name: Long natgas vs short Brent
trades.line: Nat gas +5.5% vs Brent -4.9%: own the divergence
trades.expr: Long front-month NYMEX natural gas (or UNG), short Brent futures of equal dollar notional.
trades.thesis: Crude is falling on a global surplus and a 3.4m-barrel US build, not on demand destruction; gas is a domestic winter/power story with its own tightening balance and is still sitting at only the 17th percentile of its 52-week range. The energy complex is splitting and the split is monetizable without taking a direction on oil.
trades.trigger: Natural gas +5.5% today and +10.7% on the month, trend turning up, while Brent -4.9% to 88.61 (-18.5% on the month, z=-1.92) and WTI -4.8% to 81.89 with acceleration z=-1.55.
trades.stop: Gas back below the 3.05 area (giving back the month's gain) or crude bouncing above 95 Brent; -12% on the pair.
trades.target: +20% on the pair; gas toward 3.90 while Brent holds the mid-80s.

trades.name: India over Taiwan
trades.line: Long INDA vs short EWT: new leadership vs AI unwind
trades.expr: Long INDA, short EWT, equal dollar weights.
trades.thesis: India is the only major market with positive momentum and an improving currency, and it is a net beneficiary of crude -21%. Taiwan is the concentrated expression of the semi de-rating with a currency that no longer helps. This is the cleanest way to stay invested in equities while short the AI capex trade.
trades.trigger: Sensex +10.4% on the month (z=2.46, acceleration 1.74), INDA relative strength +13.5% and turning up, USDINR -1.6% on the month; against EWT -2.3% today, -16.5% on the month (z=-2.61), TAIEX acceleration z=-2.07 and TSM -3.7%.
trades.stop: SMH reclaims its 200-day (currently 12.2% above spot) or INDA/EWT gives back 7%.

trades.name: Low vol over high beta
trades.line: Long SPLV vs short SPHB into a widening-spread tape
trades.expr: Long SPLV, short SPHB, equal dollar weights.
trades.thesis: Spread widening plus an inverted vol curve plus a 100th-percentile dollar is the textbook regime for defensives to beat beta. The high-beta/low-vol ratio has already broken trend and the market is still long momentum it has to shed.
trades.trigger: SPHB/SPLV -12.1% on the month (z=-1.92) and rolling over; MTUM z=-2.03; VIX/VIX3M inverted at 1.0111 with SKEW at z=-1.78; credit widened again today with BBB z=1.11.
trades.stop: VIX term structure back below 0.95 with HY OAS inside 3.25; -4% on the pair.

trades.name: Fuel rebate: consumer long vs E&P short
trades.line: Long XRT+ITB vs short XOP on the energy windfall
trades.expr: Long XRT and ITB (50/50), short XOP of equal total dollar notional.
trades.thesis: Crude down 21% and gasoline down 24% in a month transfers margin from producers to households and freight. E&P equity has only discounted half of it — XOP is -11.4% on the month but still +42.5% year-to-date — while retail and housing have the double tailwind of cheaper fuel and a 29bp drop in mortgage rates.
trades.trigger: Gasoline -23.6% on the month, WTI 81.89 after -4.8% today; XRT/SPY z=1.19 turning up and XHB/SPY z=1.60; mortgage 7.11% with acceleration z=-2.36; ITB +6.2% on the month.
trades.stop: Brent back above 98 (supply shock reasserts) or combined -8%.

trades.name: Short the Aussie
trades.line: Short AUDUSD: copper -12.6% month, AUD z=-1.6
trades.expr: Short AUD/USD spot at 0.6692, or buy 2-month 0.6550 AUD puts.
trades.thesis: AUD is the liquid proxy for the China/industrial-metals complex and it is trading with a 100th-percentile dollar against it. Copper, iron-ore-linked equities and the whole metals chain are in freefall; the carry no longer compensates.
trades.trigger: AUDUSD -0.7% today and -4.2% on the month (z=-1.60), AUD/JPY -3.6% on the month, copper -4.4% to 5.7115 (z=-2.02), COPX -18.3%, DXY at the 100th percentile with USDCHF and USDCAD also at 100.
trades.stop: AUDUSD back above 0.6860 or copper reclaiming 6.10; -2.5% on the position.

trades.name: Brazil washout bounce
trades.line: Long EWZ: -25.8% in a month, z=-3.33, BRL stalling
trades.expr: Buy EWZ, half size, add on a second day of BRL stability; or sell 1-month 28-strike puts to get paid for the washout.
trades.thesis: This is a currency-driven capitulation, not an earnings event. When the FX leg stops going up, the equity ETF re-rates fast because the local index only fell a third as much as the dollar-denominated ETF.
trades.trigger: USDBRL -0.1% today — the first pause after +14.1% on the month (z=3.97, acceleration 2.98); EWZ +0.3% while Bovespa -1.3%, and EWZ's one-month move is z=-3.33 at the 4th percentile of its 52-week range.
trades.stop: USDBRL takes out 6.00; or EWZ -9% from entry.
